title: Internal link path prototypes on the URL-deduplicated N=1,000 source

method.compilation: One direct tagged LuaLaTeX pass per source, using the same populated .aux and .toc seeds; no production convergence helper or .out seed.
method.audit: Compare page count, PDF tagging, link action/rectangle/contents signatures, ParentTree OBJR owners, figure alt text, and normalized extracted text.

candidates.name: direct_hyper_at_link
candidates.change: Replace the public \hyperlink call inside the page-link macro with the private \hyper@link{link}{target}{text} macro.
candidates.decision: Reject: the single pass is slower; the lower single-run RSS does not establish a memory improvement.

candidates.name: direct_hyper_at_linkstart_end
candidates.change: Replace the public link with private \hyper@linkstart and \hyper@linkend calls, retaining \Hy@xspace@end.
candidates.decision: Reject: this private entry point is slower in the single pass and offers no performance basis for production use.

candidates.name: getpagerefnumber
candidates.change: Replace \pageref*{target} with \getpagerefnumber{target}; retain the ordinary public \hyperlink macro.
candidates.decision: Reject: the single-pass difference is negligible and in the slower direction.

legacy_macro_probe.interpretation: The current tagged hyperref route does not expose the legacy pdfTeX/LuaTeX find/close macros at document start; these zero-call wrappers are not timing results. Instrument the active tagged kernel API only as a diagnostic.

limitations: Each candidate was compiled once on one machine; these are unpaired diagnostic passes, not complete converged export comparisons.
The private hyperref entry points are implementation details and were not evaluated across package versions.
ru_maxrss values are one-run child-process readings with substantial observed variation; they do not establish memory changes.
The prior pageref profile measured 0.509705 seconds over 17,590 calls, about 0.20% of a direct pass; page-number resolution is not a useful optimization target.
decision: No candidate is retained. The direct private link variants are slower, and replacing pageref* with getpagerefnumber does not measurably improve time. All three PDFs preserve the reference link annotations, their exact ParentTree OBJR owners, figure alt text, and normalized text. The N=1,000 targets of 180 seconds and 512 MiB remain unmet; further work should focus on measured tagged-link structure cost, not page-reference expansion or unprofiled legacy macros.
